title: Metric choice — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, a teammate wants a log line for every latency sample. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences comparing a log line and a metric for this need, with the cost that decides between them.

vocabulary.meaning: choosing between a log, a metric, and a trace according to the question to be answered, not according to habit
the storage and processing a signal consumes per event, which decides whether it can be recorded for every request

expectedElements: The question each signal answers is distinguished
The per-event cost is used as the deciding argument
A concrete alternative instrument is proposed
modelAnswer: Recording a log line per latency sample is the wrong instrument, because the cost per event decides here. A log line is a stored searchable record, and one per request produces millions of records whose only use is aggregation, while a metric answers the same question at a fraction of the storage. The trade-off is that a metric cannot identify which request was slow. I propose latency as a metric, with logs kept only for requests exceeding a threshold, which preserves per-request evidence.
commonMistakes: Choosing the instrument by habit rather than by cost per event
Replacing logs with metrics without keeping any way to find a slow request
variants: Rewrite the update proposing the threshold and what it would cost.
